verdicts.trueWording: LLMs introduce plot turning points earlier in the timeline
verdicts.note: Quote verbatim in Figure 1 caption of arxiv.org/html/2407.13248. Sec.4 confirms every limb: 'we observe a substantial advancement (i.e., early occurrence) of TP4 and TP5 in AI outputs... major setback (TP4) and climax (TP5)'; intro: 'notable deficiencies in narrative pacing... diminishing two key qualities: suspense and arousal'; App.: 'the major setbacks and climax arrive earlier in machine generated narratives'.

verdicts.trueWording: biased towards macro-level story-arcs, lacking narrative diversity
verdicts.note: Quote 'particularly in avoiding negative plot progressions' verbatim in the introduction, in the sentence 'machines are biased towards certain types of macro-level story-arcs and show a lack of narrative diversity, particularly in avoiding negative plot progressions.' Sec.4 gives the numbers (Riches to Rags 14.6% human vs 1.3% GPT-4).

verdicts.trueWording: Human arousal higher; gap enlarges midpoint to end; +40% over vanilla
verdicts.note: Claim carried no quote, so graded on substance. Figure 3 caption: 'Human stories consistently exhibit higher levels of suspense (greater arousal). The gap enlarges from the midpoint to the end.' Intro: 'incorporating turning point information significantly improves narrative suspense and engagement (outperforming vanilla by 40%)'; abstract says 'over 40% improvement'. Note the 40% is a human comparative win-rate (Table 4: suspense-best 7.9% Outline-Only vs 48.3% +Self TP), not a rating scale.

verdicts.trueWording: As map scale increases, plans skip steps, keeping high-level structure
verdicts.note: Quote 'output plans tend to skip steps, leading to failure cases' verbatim at arxiv.org/html/2506.10161 Sec.IV-B: 'As the map scale increases, output plans tend to skip steps, leading to failure cases. These failed plans often maintain a correct high-level structure.' The more-characters limb: 'increasing the number of adventurers leads to plans that skip steps while maintaining reasonable high-level structure.'

verdicts.trueWording: most failed plans causally sound, actions lacking valid intention
verdicts.note: Quote 'character actions lacking valid intention' verbatim. Full page sentence: 'For the o1 model, most failed plans are causally sound, but often with character actions lacking valid intention. For instance, Aladdin kills the dragon due to perceived threat but then obtains the lamp and casts a spell without valid motivation.' Two qualifiers the claim drops but does not contradict: the finding is scoped to the o1 model on the Aladdin intentional-planning task, and the page says 'often with', not always.

verdicts.trueWording: shortcuts for conflict: adventurer snakebitten or self-healing, no other characters
verdicts.note: Claim carried no quote. Page (Sec.IV-B, western/conflict domain): 'We observe other types of attempts to create shortcuts for conflict, such as an adventurer repeatedly getting snakebites or healing themselves to cause medicine shortage without involving other characters.' Page has 'or healing themselves' where the claim has 'and healing himself'. The 'rather than clashing commitment frames' limb is supported in substance: Sec.II-B defines conflict as arising 'between commitment frames', and the shortcut is expressly 'without involving other characters'.

verdicts.trueWording: drops are in western conflict-planning with adventurers, not intentional planning
verdicts.note: The numbers are real and verbatim-adjacent, but attached to the wrong experiment. Page: 'Figure 3(c) displays the o1 model's performance on WESTERN variations with varying numbers of adventurers... The success rate drops sharply from 2 to 3 adventurers (likely due to handling multi-party conflicts) and from 10 to 12 adventurers (likely due to exceeding context limits).' The western/adventurer variations are the CONFLICT-planning domain; intentional planning is the Aladdin delegation-network experiment (Figure 3(b)), whose reported driver is added delegation layers, not adventurer count. Second limb is supported: abstract says 'planning with character intentionality and dramatic conflict remains challenging, requiring LLMs trained with reinforcement learning for complex reasoning.'
verdicts.unsupportedLimb: the attribution of the 2-to-3 and 10-to-12 adventurer drops to intentional planning; the page reports them for the western dramatic-conflict variations

verdicts.trueWording: Narrators explicitly explain the theme 77% versus 52% for humans
verdicts.note: Quote verbatim at arxiv.org/html/2604.03136: 'The pattern is one of over-determination: AI spells out meaning rather than trusting the reader to infer it.' Preceding sentence: 'Narrators explicitly explain the story's theme 77% of the time, versus 52% for humans.' Corpus size confirmed: '10,272 writing prompts, each written by a human author and five LLMs... yielding 61,608 stories'.

verdicts.trueWording: conveys emotion through physical sensations and bodily metaphors (81% vs. 38%)
verdicts.note: Quote verbatim: 'AI overwhelmingly conveys emotion through physical sensations and bodily metaphors (81% vs. 38% human), deploys more smell-based imagery (82% vs. 57%).' Both figures match the claim exactly.

verdicts.trueWording: far fewer subplots (79% no subplots vs. 57%); resolutions 69% vs. 46%
verdicts.note: Quote verbatim (curly quotes in source): 'AI stories exhibit tighter causal chains, more protagonist-driven resolutions (69% vs. 46%), and far fewer subplots (79% “no subplots” vs. 57%).' All three limbs on the page in one sentence.

verdicts.trueWording: AI sticks to vague allusions, avoids naming real brands, places, or works
verdicts.note: Quote verbatim: 'whereas AI generally sticks to vague allusions and avoids naming real brands, places, or works.' Same sentence: 'Humans reference specific texts and authors at nearly double the AI rate (47% vs. 24%).' The 72% vs 50% allusion figure is on the page one paragraph earlier: 'references to other works tend to be vague allusions (72% vs. 50%)'.

verdicts.trueWording: present morally ambivalent protagonists more often (59% vs. 38%)
verdicts.note: Quote verbatim: 'Human stories draw from a broader narrative repertoire: they span more locations, carry more dialogue relative to narration, integrate more subplots into overarching themes (42% vs. 21%), and present morally ambivalent protagonists more often (59% vs. 38%).' All three limbs are in that one sentence.

verdicts.trueWording: AI resolutions favor internal understanding or acceptance (47% vs. 27%)
verdicts.note: Quote verbatim: 'AI resolutions favor internal understanding or acceptance (47% vs. 27%), whereas humans are more comfortable with ambiguous endings.'

verdicts.trueWording: human stories occupy a rarer, more dispersed region of narrative space
verdicts.note: Quote 'Human narratives are rarer.' is verbatim (a paragraph heading in Sec.4 and in the contents list). Conclusion: 'human stories show greater structural diversity and occupy a rarer, more dispersed region of narrative space'; dispersion measured ('Human stories are also more dispersed'; mean rarity percentile 0.71 vs 0.49). Detection limb: 'narrative features alone achieve 93.2% macro-F1 for human vs. AI detection'.

verdicts.trueWording: without further specification of style or substance, output feels generic
verdicts.note: Quote verbatim at arxiv.org/html/2402.18659v5 (stamped 'arXiv:2402.18659v5 [cs.CL] 09 Dec 2024'), Sec.III-D: 'Prompting current LLMs for stories, without any further specification of style or substance, tends to produce output that feels generic.' The claim restates that sentence.
